changes: First build researched for this wiki (the research notes on the [Mechanics reference](/mechanics-reference) quote this build).

evidence: Normal is no longer the plain defaults: fewer pests (×0.7), pest HP ×0.65, enemy damage ×0.55, boss and elite HP ×0.65, Tibo max HP ×1.5, XP ×1.3, 1 extra revive, enemy tiers lag 2 minutes and fewer wall pests (×0.3). POI charge sounds can overlap (up to 4 voices).

changes: Balance pass: many base weapons and evolutions hit harder, Butter Streak cooldown 3.5 → 2.5 s, proc items roughly doubled, Boom Spud 8% → 12%, Spud Freezer freezes every enemy for 7.5 s.
evidence: Balance pass. changes: Hard and Nightmare get much easier: Hard nearly matches Normal and Nightmare is far gentler; both lag enemy tiers 2 minutes. Dogs are Legendary 1/3 of the time (was 1/6). P pauses.
evidence: Hard and Nightmare are much easier. Hard now nearly matches Normal (pests ×0.75, pest HP ×0.65, damage ×0.6, boss HP ×0.7, max HP ×1.5, XP ×1.3); Nightmare drops to pests ×1.05, pest HP ×1.2, damage ×0.95, boss HP ×0.95, elite HP ×1.3 and gains max HP ×1.2. Both now lag enemy tiers by 2 minutes and their opening crowds ramp up later. Dogs are Legendary twice as often (1/3, was 1/6). Adds a P key to pause.

changes: Outside Story, a revive plays the knock-down scene, then Tibo gets up with 50% HP and 2 s of invulnerability. Screen clears take 5% from bosses (was 25%).
evidence: The main game config, story script and a few tables moved from the sim chunk to the boot chunk; the wiki now finds them in either. Revives outside Story play the same knocked-down scene as Story, then Tibo gets up with 50% HP and 2 s of invulnerability; level-ups earned while down wait until then. Screen clears (`nuke` weapons such as Reset Button) now take only 5% from bosses (was 25%). Armor, dodge and crit item and passive descriptions no longer show point values. Game data otherwise unchanged.

changes: Nightmare: late damage ramp starts at 5:00 (was 15:00), 20% fewer snacks, new boss bullet patterns. Vampire Tot heals 0.05 HP per kill (was 0.15). Adds an Update game button.
evidence: Nightmare's late damage ramp now starts at 5:00 instead of 15:00, adding 0.064 per minute instead of 0.2. Snacks drop 20% less often on Nightmare (normal pests 0.32%, Crop Patches 28%); their healing is unchanged. Nightmare adds alternate bullet patterns for amusing, Colorado Queen, The Masher, Late Blight, Sir Strawman, The Fryer King, Blight Spore and Ice Imp. Vampire Tot heals 0.05 HP per kill (was 0.15); Hash Bulwark's guard burst rises from 72 to 86. Meteor Russet delays its triggering hit by 0.4 s; the area blast lands at the original trigger position (see its item page for target and capacity rules). Story's starting-kit offer now waits for the current line's reading time. Refreshes meteor, projectile-trail, landmark, ground and evolution visuals. The difficulty table changes its internal balance targets to `mixReach`; these are not measured survival rates. Icons are unchanged.

changes: Curses bring extra bosses half as often (×0.25, was ×0.5): the first needs four curses. Nightmare hides enemy shot-path markers. Peel Forest has fewer props (12 per chunk, was 20).

Improves sprite texture packing and updates the in-game changelog. Other content values, English content descriptions, difficulty multipliers, simulation logic and wiki icons are unchanged.

changes: Outside Story, revives give 4 s of invulnerability (was 2), push enemies harder, freeze pests for 5 s, slow bosses and clear nearby shots. Ice Imp's Nightmare fan speeds up from 85 to 130.
evidence: Outside Story, revives now grant 4 s of invulnerability (was 2), push nearby visible pests and bosses with strength 900 in a 160-unit radius plus their body radius (was pests only, strength 400 within 120), freeze pests and elites for 5 s, slow bosses to 50% speed for 5 s and delay their next pattern, and clear shots within 160 units. Expands the in-game changelog, including notes for older releases. English content descriptions, difficulty multipliers and wiki icons are unchanged.

changes: Nightmare adds larger ground attacks for the Masher, Late Blight and the Fryer King. Outside Story, loot without a choice shows as icon notices while play continues.
evidence: Nightmare adds larger ground attacks centred on Tibo's position: the Masher strikes a disk and two rings 0.35 s apart, Late Blight places a central pool plus six satellite pools, and the Fryer King strikes six wedges in alternating sets 0.5 s apart, leaving oil puddles after the second set. One Story lasso line now suggests asking a Grok Bot for directions. Other balance values, English content descriptions and wiki icons are unchanged.

changes: Tater Slots wins add bonus gold: three of a kind adds four spin prices, a pair half a spin price. New weapon and item effects. Shared-run pages hide scores for some capped runs.
evidence: Tater Slots now adds gold to both winning outcomes: three of a kind gives a 1-reward chest plus four current spin prices of bonus gold; a pair gives a random item plus half a spin price, rounded to the nearest gold. The bonus is calculated at payout and is not multiplied by gold gain. Adds glints to held weapons, trails and launch flashes to on-hurt item shots, firing flashes/sparks/casings for Fry Sentry, Fry Brigade and Tater Pup, and sparkle/shatter effects for Hash Brown Shield and Hash Bulwark. Healing, pickup and reward rings use sharper pixel-sized bands. Shared-run pages withhold reconstructed scores for capped kill totals, peak enemy counts above 550 or capped source damage in runs shorter than 90 minutes. Startup, retry and shared-run loading code moves between chunks without changing those rules. Other balance values, English content descriptions, difficulty settings and wiki icons are unchanged.

changes: Japanese text uses Japanese fonts installed on the device and sits centred on buttons. Tilt-shift keeps faint details sharp. No gameplay changes.
evidence: Japanese labels now use Japanese fonts installed on the device, with adjusted vertical alignment to centre text on buttons. Tilt-shift rendering now mixes the original scene back into low-alpha pixels to keep those details sharp. Enemy shots use the post-processing blend mode whenever the scene renders to an offscreen target, including tilt-shift without bloom. Game data, English content descriptions, difficulty settings and wiki icons are unchanged. Simulation functions are reordered and renamed without changing their formulas. The Tater Slots jackpot change belongs to game version 19, despite its position in the in-game changelog.

changes: Sir Strawman's sickles slow and return; his Nightmare fan launches at 130 (was 120) without curving in. More crisp pixel-art effects; poteto and Alex cutscenes play on slow connections.
evidence: Sir Strawman's seven sickles now slow and return along their heading; Nightmare's fan launches at 130 instead of 120 and no longer curves inward. Returning bullet speed is ×0.7 on Easy, ×1.05 on Normal, Hard and Nightmare (Story ×1); outward speed is unaffected. More effects use crisp pixel art: boss attacks, warning rings, lasso trails, Grok Bots, visitor stun/landing effects, pickups, pools, buildings and ambient dust. Late-loaded poteto and Alex cutscenes now play on slow connections. Cards refit after language fonts load, multilingual text has more room, and the Moldy Shrine menu is shorter with a corrected extra-boss forecast; curse rewards and spawn rules are unchanged. World generation checks nearby cells first and computes sin/cos together without changing the sampled output. Performance telemetry adds median frame work time. Other content tables, English content descriptions and wiki icons are unchanged.

changes: Tibo's hit circle for enemy shots grows from radius 2.5 to 4 and moves 2.72 units down towards his feet. New effects for Hot Potato, chain arcs and revives.
evidence: Tibo's enemy-shot hit circle grows from 2.5 to 4 units in radius and moves 2.72 units down towards his feet. Near-miss and bullet-culling distances use the shifted centre too; homing still aims at his unshifted position. Contact and pickup radii are unchanged. The displayed hit circle follows the new position. Adds fuse sparks and heat flashes to Hot Potato and Spicy Hot Potato, distinct pixel-art arcs for Starch Chain, Gratin Arc, Starch Supercell and Grok Bots, sharper Steam Vent and Pressure Cooker rings, and a new revive burst. The in-game changelog adds the hit-circle change and a note about earlier boss/enemy art. Other content values, English content descriptions, difficulty settings and wiki icons are unchanged.

changes: Sprite rendering is reworked and bright ground effects are slightly darker. No gameplay changes.
evidence: Sprite rendering switches to power-of-two texture-sheet heights and sprite-local texture coordinates, with sampling snapped to a 1/8192-texel grid. Outlines, shadows, projectile sprites and ghost dithering use the local coordinates too. Bright interiors of ground effects are darker and their added glow is slightly reduced. The debug sheetrows URL option now accepts only positive powers of two. The in-game changelog adds a note about notices, such as a dog joining the pack, being centred with the controls hint. Simulation logic, content values, English content descriptions, difficulty settings and wiki icons are unchanged.

changes: No gameplay changes; the in-game changelog regroups seven older notes under release ec984b0.
evidence: The in-game changelog moves seven existing notes from its next section into release ec984b0, dated 2026-11-03: world effects, Sir Strawman's returning sickles, slow-connection Story reveals, font-loading card refits, Chinese/Japanese/Korean text fit, Moldy Shrine menu fit, and Indic/Thai card marks. These are older notes being grouped, not new gameplay changes in this build. Game data, English content descriptions, difficulty settings, simulation and rendering logic, and wiki icons are unchanged.

changes: New game versions can load automatically on the Reset screen or between runs, keeping your difficulty. Boss death blasts get new sprites. No gameplay changes.
evidence: New game versions can load automatically on the idle Reset screen and before starting another non-Story run from the end screen, preserving the selected difficulty for up to 60 s. A session-storage guard prevents repeated automatic reloads into the same offered build; shared-run parameters are cleared on reload. Update checks also run on the stats screen and use /version.json. Boss death blasts now use two pixel-scaled sprite tiers, sparkles and a separate ground ring; small effect strokes remain visible when downscaled. Rendering caches unchanged overlapping-pool outlines and terrain sample indices, preserves the sharp image when blur is zero, and reports more specific graphics-fallback causes and browser/device categories. The changelog adds the automatic-update note, groups four older notes under earlier releases, and adjusts its narrow layout. Combat data, English content descriptions, difficulty settings, simulation logic and wiki icons are unchanged.

changes: HUD layout measures sliding banners at their resting positions. No gameplay changes.
evidence: HUD safe-space measurements now subtract sliding banners' CSS translations, including translated ancestors, so layout uses their resting positions instead of their animated positions. This applies to both fresh and cached measurements. The renderer adds an optional half-rate sun-shadow update path, but it defaults off and this build has no caller enabling it; normal shadow updates are unchanged. Shared-run encoding only renames local variables; analytics and the end screen record the new game commit. Combat logic, content values, English content descriptions, difficulty settings and wiki icons are unchanged.

changes: At most 2 shooting pests before 3:00 and 4 before 6:00. Great Wireworm fires one five-shot fan. Moldy Shrine gold grows faster over time. Unusable Spud Whetstones vanish.
evidence: Ordinary pest spawns allow at most two shooters before 3:00 and four before 6:00, then return to the cap of 30. Great Wireworm fires one wider five-shot fan instead of two bursts; its click-beetle shots slow, aim once at Tibo after 0.9 s and accelerate, with earlier retargeting at 0.72 s and a faster finish on Nightmare. Moldy Shrine gold becomes round((45 + 20 × minutes + 2 × minutes²) × gold gain), up from 45 + 9 × minutes before gold gain. Unused Spud Whetstones vanish when weapon slots are full, no eligible weapon can level and no union is currently available; newly generated chunks omit them until that condition clears. Dogs stop pointing at vanished whetstones. Adds Game updated changelog notices after update reloads, a pausing HUD changelog button for relaunched runs, and collapsible older changelog dates. Browsers without WebGL 2 get an explanatory screen with a copyable link instead of the low-detail game. Story reading time excludes pauses and overlays, and reduced-motion lesson panels refit around the cards. Overlapping pools of the same kind share outlines; shot-path previews use thin rose arrows (still hidden on Nightmare). Adds crisp weapon/item effects, dog dash and scent trails, pickup trails/sparkles and revised landing/frost rings. Analytics adds average enemy counts; clipboard, browser detection and card helpers move between chunks. Other content values, English content descriptions, difficulty multipliers and wiki icons are unchanged.

changes: Dog abilities get new ground marks, sparkles and dust; herd gusts glow brighter. No gameplay changes.
evidence: Dog abilities gain ground marks and sparkles: bite impact rings, herd dust rings, bark echoes, fetch stars, dig holes and rescue dust puffs. Herd gusts glow more brightly, add glints and spread more dust; gusts and dust fade behind Tibo to keep him visible. These effects respect reduced-motion, flashes and effects-opacity settings. Simulation logic, content values, English content descriptions, difficulty settings and wiki icons are unchanged.

changes: Item bags and healing snacks get new sprites, glow, idle animations and pickup bursts. No gameplay changes.
evidence: Item bags and healing snacks get new sprites, coloured glow halos and sparkles. Item bags hop while idle and shake as they charge; snacks pulse. Opening a bag throws confetti, while collecting a snack scatters leaves; both add brief sparkles and a fading halo. Reduced motion uses still poses, and disabling flashes dims burst light and skips the brightest bag-flare frames. The sprite atlas is repacked; other sprite frames and wiki icons are unchanged. Simulation logic, content values, English content descriptions and difficulty settings are unchanged.

changes: Railgun beams get new pixel art with a travelling pulse; scorch marks glow slightly brighter. No gameplay changes.
evidence: Railgun beams now use direction-matched pixel tiles instead of rotated strips, with a bright pulse travelling along the beam; reduced motion skips the pulse. The main renderer compensates for perspective, and the debug renderer snaps the tiles to its pixel grid. Beam scorch marks glow slightly brighter. The sprite atlas is repacked; only the railgun core frames change, and wiki icons are unchanged. The in-game changelog groups eleven existing notes under the older game commit 445c881 rather than treating them as new changes. Simulation logic, content values, English content descriptions and difficulty settings are unchanged.

changes: Better graphics recovery: interrupted downloads pause and retry, and a failed 3D scene retries on Low. Chest evolution halos become gold rings. No gameplay changes.
evidence: Interrupted 3D scene downloads now pause play and retry with delays growing from 1 to 8 s; failed early sprite-page downloads can retry too. After a graphics reset, the renderer waits up to 5 s for restoration, then tries a fresh context before falling back. A scene-construction failure retries 3D once on Low at half resolution without adaptive quality; a second construction failure still uses the 2D fallback. Active intro/landing cutscenes end as skipped if the renderer stops being ready. Chest evolution halos use layered gold ground rings with eight rotating dashes instead of three size-specific sprite animations; reduced motion keeps the ring still. The late atlas drops those three clips and repacks the remaining unchanged frames. Adds a translated graphics-recovery changelog note. Combat simulation, existing content/config values, English content descriptions, difficulty settings and wiki icons are unchanged.

changes: Elite pests break apart in new death animations. Fryer King and Late Blight puddles bubble; Root Tunnel gets an animated exit hole. No gameplay changes.
evidence: Elite pests now break apart in pixel-art death animations with detached gold-rim fragments, in both the main and debug renderers. The main renderer loads separate elite-death and glint sheets through the effects worker, with a main-thread fallback; missing art keeps the ordinary death animation. Fryer King and Late Blight puddles have redrawn, slower surfaces and new boiling bubbles; reduced motion holds the surface and bubble poses still. Root Tunnel gains a closing exit hole and animated clods that bounce and fall back in, with simpler reduced-motion poses; Tibo's outline is hidden while sinking. Shared effects helpers move into separate or consuming chunks, and effect sprites gain horizontal-flip support. Adds a translated elite-death changelog note. Combat simulation is byte-identical after asset-name changes; registry values, extracted gameplay settings, English content descriptions, difficulty settings and wiki icons are unchanged.

changes: Charging pests kick up dust; Wandering Eyes and All-Seeing Spud shots get new animations. No gameplay changes.
evidence: Charging pests kick up dust and bouncing grit when they launch and stop, and leave a dust trail during a charge, in both the main and debug renderers; reduced motion hides these effects. Wandering Eyes and All-Seeing Spud shots gain directional turning poses, glancing eyes, trails, glow and impact pops in the main renderer. Reduced motion suppresses their trails and holds impact poses; disabling flashes skips the brightest impact frame. The early sprite atlas adds those animations and repacks unchanged frames; All-Seeing Spud's dot sprite is redrawn. The atlas-band worker can queue 16 unacknowledged bands instead of 4, without changing its pixel painting. Combat simulation is byte-identical after asset-name changes; content values, extracted gameplay settings, English text, difficulty settings, late-atlas frames and wiki icons are unchanged.

changes: Link and Zelda & Link show stored fluff as orbiting tufts; Zelda's marks gain moons and clocks; Frenzy Fryer gets a new gold ring. No gameplay changes.
evidence: Link and Zelda & Link show stored fluff as orbiting tufts, with a pop and outward wisps when a charge is spent. Zelda's ordinary pest marks gain moons, remaining-time clocks and rising stars, separate from eclipse marks. Reduced motion holds the fluff and moons still and hides mark stars; disabling flashes suppresses the mark pop and blinking. Both renderers replace the frenzy ring sprite with a gold ring, rotating chevrons and streaks that accelerate in the final 6 seconds and fade in the final second; reduced motion freezes the ring. The late atlas adds 11 companion-effect clips; the early atlas drops the old frenzy ring and shrinks from 1664 to 1536 pixels high. All retained atlas clips and wiki icons are pixel-identical. The in-game changelog moves an existing graphics-recovery note into a versioned wave and defers older entries. Combat simulation is identical after asset-name changes; gameplay data, English content, difficulty values, workers and audio worklets are unchanged.

changes: Tibo's hitbox circle shows by default (size unchanged). The 2D renderer is removed. With analytics on, top-scoring runs are sent for a replay check. New mine warning rings.
evidence: Tibo's hitbox circle is on by default, lime and thicker, with a smaller stroke in narrow views; settings saved before version 3 turn it on once. Its collision radius and position are unchanged. The flat 2D renderer and renderer URL choice are removed: repeated crashes start lean 3D on Low at half resolution. Failed graphics recovery now stops play and offers Reload or Copy link instead of falling back to 2D; scene-download retries and context restoration remain. With analytics consent and run/session IDs, qualifying high-score or cap-invalid runs submit their shared run, stats and input log to /replay; this review verifies the client path, not server replay. Mine warning rings become procedural, with lamps that react to nearby enemies and the remaining fuse, quieter overlapping rings and reduced-motion/flash handling; Low quality uses simpler rings. Rendering, pixel-effect baking, chest/jackpot and camera helpers are reorganized into new or merged modules. The early atlas replaces two mine-ring clips with two lamp clips; all 666 retained early clips, all 1,252 late clips and wiki icons are pixel-identical. The changelog adds hitbox, lean-3D and replay notes, and groups an existing elite-death note under its older version; translations add the stopped-graphics text and wording fixes. Combat simulation retains the same statements after consistent binding renames and removal of two helpers with no simulation callers. Gameplay definitions, English content, difficulty values, workers and audio worklets are unchanged.

changes: Adds nine base weapons, each with an evolution (93 weapons total): Gem Sling, Hot Streak, Locked Gatling, Mash Snowball, Seed Potato, Spud Fence, Tailgate Fries, Tater Twirl, Tot Stampede.
evidence: Adds nine base weapons—Gem Sling, Hot Streak, Locked Gatling, Mash Snowball, Seed Potato, Spud Fence, Tailgate Fries, Tater Twirl and Tot Stampede—and one evolution for each (93 weapons total). changes: Adds Andrew, a visitor once per run between 18:00 and 22:00. Standing in his shrinking gold ring for 20 s gives 15% faster weapon timers (×1.61 with Frenzy Fryer).
evidence: Adds Andrew, a visitor scheduled once per run between 18:00 and 22:00. He pairs for 20 seconds: standing inside his gold ring gives 15% faster weapon timers, multiplying with Frenzy Fryer to ×1.61. changes: Ketchup Kraken fires one five-blob fan instead of two nine-shot fans; the blobs slow down and become damaging puddles, larger on higher difficulties.

Their damage rate is 2.8 times the shot's scaled damage per second, applied every 0.5 s. Adds animated ketchup-blob art and a translated changelog note. evidence: The HUD shows base icons before expansion icons finish loading, then refreshes newly available weapon/passive icons and loot banners.
